The processing method provided in this paper is of great significance for improving the quality of the air film holes in the blades and, thus, has an important reference value for extending the service life of aero engines.
II. EXPERIMENTAL PROCEDURES
A. Materials

The experimental material is GH3536, a nickel-based superalloy commonly employed in high-pressure turbine blades of aviation engines. The sample dimensions are 25×25×0.8mm3,andthe surfaces of the samples were cleaned with ethanol before the experiment. The main chemical composition of the GH3536 nickelbased superalloy is shown in Table I.
B. Equipment and helical drilling principle

The test platform consists of a five-axis_CNC machine tool integrated with a femtosecond laser, a reflector box, a helical drilling optical system, a water-cooling system, an auxiliary gas-blowing device, and a control mainframe, as illustrated in Fig. 1. The reflector box directs the light beam from the femtosecond laser into the helical drilling system, while the water-cooling system dissipates heat to maintain stable light emission from the femtosecond laser.The software on the control mainframe regulates the mirror offset,

the rotational speed of the hollow motor, and the deflection angle of the wedge prism. Thefemtosecond laser is the TruMicro 203manufactured by TRUMPF of Germany. Its main parameters are shown in Table II.

The helical drilling system consists of a series of components, including parallel mirrors, half-wave plates, wedge prisms,hollow motors, Dove prisms, balanced mirrors, andfocusing mirrors. The trajectory of the laser beam is illustrated in Fig. 2.The femtosecond laser beam is first reflected by mirror M1and then passes through a half-wave plate, producing linearly polarized light. It is subsequently reflected by mirror M2 and directed through a wedge prism,which deflects the beam. The deflected beam then enters the Dove prism,which is in high-speed rotation, resulting in the high-speed rotation of the laser beam. The rotational speed of the Dove prism can be adjusted between 1600and 5000 rpm. In the experiment,the rotational speed we used was 2000rpm. The high-speed rotating laser beam passes through a balanced mirror system and is focused by a focusing mirror, producing a laser beam suitable for processing. The laser beam propagation path in the helical drilling optical system is shown in Fig. 2.

The mirror M2 and wedge prism are mounted on a platform capable of translating in both directions. The platform's displacement is precisely controlled by software within the mainframe. This displacement influences the incident position of the beam before it enters thefocusing mirror,thereby determining the taper of the small hole. The bidirectional platform has a displacement range of -4 to 4mm,and varying displacements result in different hole tapers, as illustrated in Fig. 3.

The mobile platform is also equipped with a motor to adjust the rotation angle of the wedge prism, with the angle being precisely controlled by the software in the mainframe. The rotation angle determines the laser beam's angle of incidence on the focusing mirror, which in turn affects the aperture of the small hole. The rotation angle of the wedge prism ranges from -27° to 27°, and the working principle of the wedge prism is shown in Fig. 4.
